name: Core World
desc: You grew up in the heart of what remains of civilization. Vast data-nets, towering arcologies, and complex social hierarchies define life here. Air filtered, water pure, dangers hidden behind polite smiles and corporate logos. You know how to work the system: which bureaucrat to charm, which archive code unlocks restricted tech. Your social networks are your lifeline — powerful and demanding, but essential to surviving the maze.

feature.name: Institutional Leverage
feature.text:
The Core Worlds run on bureaucracy and influence, and you know which doors open to which knocks.
- **Trigger.** The first time each scene you work through an institution for a permit, restricted file, credential, or formal access.
- **Roll.** Make one Presence or Knowledge Roll, DC 15, chosen by the declared approach.
- **Effect.** On any success, gain **1 Favor Token** up to your cap; a Critical Success grants no second Token. Before rolling a later noncombat institutional task at DC 20 or lower in the same category, spend 1 Favor to treat it as Success with Hope. It cannot defeat an opposed character, bypass a Tier restriction, or alter dice already rolled.
- **Uses and refresh.** Favor Tokens are the galaxy's single social currency (the Diplomat's class resource, Chapters 6 and 7, is the same Token). Tokens are kept until spent. A non-Diplomat from a Core World holds up to **2** of them at a time, earned through this benefit. A **Diplomat** from a Core World folds these into their class pool instead: their maximum Favor Tokens rises to **6** (from the base 4), and they begin each session with **1 extra** on top of their normal starting Tokens. Either way it is one pool, not two.

name: Trade Hub
desc: You were raised in the chaotic symphony of a bazaar. The air smells of spices, ozone, and the quiet desperation of those with nothing left to trade. Your market intuition sniffs out profit or disaster a parsec away. Your information networks are gossip, shipping manifests, the whispers of black-market dealers. You learned young that knowing what's about to happen is worth more than owning what's already happening.

feature.name: Market Oracle
feature.text:
You know how to read the currents of trade.
- **Trigger.** Negotiating prices or seeking information about goods, gambling resources on rumors.
- **Roll.** Knowledge (DC 10).
- **Effect.** A piece of true, actionable information *and* 1 path resource (Hope if Awakened, Effort progress if Sleeping). On a Critical Success, a secret that grants Advantage on related rolls for **24 hours**.
- **On a failure.** The resource went to a bad rumor and you gain nothing; the Keeper may use the failed attempt as a story hook.

name: Frontier Colony
desc: Your home was grit, rust, and shared hardship. Neighbors would share their last water ration without a second thought. Practical ingenuity is your creed. Can you MacGyver a comms array from a broken toaster and some solar cells? Of course. Bonds run deep, but so do obligations. If you owe Old Man Jax a favor on Persephone's Reach, you pay it. The frontier teaches that the only insurance against the next disaster is the people who survived the last one.

feature.name: Scrap-Savvy Ingenuity
feature.text:
You can improvise tools and simple devices from junk.
- **Trigger.** Improvising a tool or simple device from scrap.
- **Roll.** Make a **Knowledge (Tech) Roll, DC 10**.
- **Effect.** On success, the device works reliably for the scene. On Failure with Hope, it works once and then fails safely. On Failure with Fear, it does not work and the chosen scrap is consumed. Matching dice are a Critical Success and also produce one additional useful function agreed before the Roll.
- **Uses and refresh.** Once per Long Rest, after a nonmatching result and before narration, sacrifice a sentimental personal item built into the project to reroll the Hope die; use the new face and resolve the complete Roll again.

name: Void Station
desc: You grew up in a pressurized can hurtling through nothing. Claustrophobic? Maybe. But you breathed recycled air alongside a dozen species. Technical adaptation is instinct — you feel when the oxygen scrubbers are unhappy by their hum. Cultural fluency is a second language: trade insults with a Kryllian miner at dawn, sip tea with a Celestiari diplomat by afternoon. Void Station natives understand every other being is just trying to get through the day.

feature.name: Cross-Species Intuition
feature.text:
Your upbringing has made you adept at understanding different perspectives.
- **Uses.** You begin each session with **3 Linguistic Tokens**.
- **Trigger.** A negotiation roll.
- **Effect.** Spend 1 token to **reroll a Hope die**, or to **treat your Fear die as a Hope die** for that roll.
- **Timing.** Declare a token after the dice land but before the Keeper narrates the outcome. A reroll replaces the Hope die's value; treating your Fear die as a Hope die leaves the total unchanged and makes the roll Hope-dominant. Recalculate total and dominance afterward; a Critical Success still requires the dice to actually match.
- **Refresh.** Regain all spent tokens by mediating a faction dispute, or after a long rest.

name: Free Fleet
tag: Family Found in the Deep Black
desc: Home is not a place. It is the next jump. Stellar navigation is in your bones. You navigate pulsar fields like others walk city streets. Fleet solidarity is your creed. That scar on your shoulder matches your crewmate's. You find family not in blood but in shared experience of the deep black. Free Fleet natives know your crew is your tribe, ships are alive in ways planets cannot be, and the best people are those who learned to live in motion.

feature.name: Voidborn Kinship
feature.text:
You share a deep bond with your fellow travelers.
- **Trigger.** Recalling information about stellar hazards, or aiding allies from your fleet (any crew you have traveled with for more than a tenday).
- **Effect.** Reroll a single failed Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Roll; *or* let an ally in your system **use your Hope die result as their own** for one roll, transferring your moment of fortune into their hands.

name: AgriSynth
desc: You were born beneath the soft, pulsing glow of nutrient lamps. Your first breath was air scrubbed by great AgriSynth processors. The rhythm of life was set by the silent, omnipresent Harvest-Minds — vast AI networks managing every aspect of food production. You understand biology as someone who grew up watching it managed by intelligent systems: pattern, cycle, intervention, harvest. You know when a field is healthy and when something is wrong.

feature.name: Nourished by Nature
feature.text:
Your sterile but life-focused upbringing gave you a unique understanding of biology.
- **Effect.** **Advantage on Knowledge (Medicine) Rolls to stabilize creatures near death**, and **Advantage on Instinct Rolls to find or purify food and water**.
- **The limit.** The Survival edge applies only in technologically-supported environments (stations, ships, settled worlds with infrastructure). On a wild planet without automation, your training does not translate cleanly.

name: The Displaced Enclave
desc: You grew up in one of the hidden Ailuran enclaves — stations, asteroid warrens, or camouflaged surface settlements that existed in the margins for longer than most civilizations have records. Your childhood was vertical: narrow towers, deep shafts, climbing routes, the sound of claws on metal as the heartbeat of daily life. Privacy was sacred. Then the Veil Rip dissolved your cloaking, and the galaxy saw you. Yours chose to step forward.
restriction: Ailuran-specific. A non-Ailuran character cannot select Displaced Enclave; the cultural specifics do not translate. Ailurans may also select any of the other six communities.

feature.name: Ghost Protocol
feature.text:
You were raised in a culture that elevated concealment to an art form.
- **Uses.** Once per session.
- **Effect.** Declare one plausible preparation your prior access allowed: an escape route to one known adjacent zone; a cache containing one Common (TT1) item worth at most 4 Cr; or a fallback position granting Light Cover to the crew in one current zone. The player states the exact route, item, or position. It cannot cross a sealed barrier, contradict an established fact, resolve a Clock, or create unavailable technology.
- **The edge.** If your Class Feature grants reconnaissance training, choose one additional detail: a keycard for one established Common lock, the next guard rotation's timing, or Disadvantage on one surveillance attempt against the crew before the scene ends.
